title: God, from Whom All Blessings Flow
description: God, from Whom All Blessings Flow in Tonic Solfa to MARTYN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 913 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “For Union of Heart”, where the book credits them to the Methodist Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens Double (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MARTYN; any other Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: God, from whom all bless-ings flow, Per-fect-ing the saints be-low, Hear us, who thy na-ture share, Who thy lov-ing child-ren are. Join us, in one spir-it join, Let us still re-ceive of thine: Still for more on thee we call, Thou who fil-lest all in all!

lines: God, from whom all blessings flow,
Perfecting the saints below,
Hear us, who thy nature share,
Who thy loving children are.
Join us, in one spirit join,
Let us still receive of thine:
Still for more on thee we call,
Thou who fillest all in all!
Closer knit us to our Head;
Nourish us, in Christ, and feed;
Let us daily growth receive,
More and more in Jesus live.
Move, and actuate, and guide;
Divers gifts to each divide:
Placed according to thy will,
Let us all our work fulfil;
Sweetly may we all agree,
Touched with softest sympathy;
Kindly for each other care;
Every member feel its share.
Love, like death, hath all destroyed,
Rendered our distinctions void!
Names, and sects, and parties fall:
Thou, O God, art all in all!

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MARTYN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
